faqs.a: Duotone is a print-era technique where an image is reproduced with exactly two inks. Digitally, every pixel's brightness is remapped between a dark color (shadows) and a bright color (highlights). Spotify's famous artist images use dark green-black shadows with vivid green highlights.
faqs.q: What exactly is a duotone effect?

faqs.a: Shadows control how the darkest parts of the photo look; highlights control the brightest parts. For a classic look, pick a near-black shadow and a vivid brand color as the highlight.

faqs.a: Portraits and high-contrast photos work best because the brightness map has clear darks and lights. Very flat or washed-out images produce muddy results — increase contrast first with an equalizer tool.

duotone-effect.formula:
gray = 0.299 x R + 0.587 x G + 0.114 x B
t = gray / 255
duotone = shadow + (highlight - shadow) x t
final = gray + (duotone - gray) x (strength / 100)
Example: gray = 76, shadow = (25, 20, 20), highlight = (29, 185, 84), t = 0.30
duotone R = 25 + (29 - 25) x 0.30 = 26.2.

keyFacts: Duotone remaps every pixel's brightness between two colors: dark tones become the shadow color, bright tones become the highlight color.
The default pair (#191414 / #1DB954) recreates the iconic Spotify artist-image look.
Six curated presets: Spotify green, sunset, ocean, noir, rose, and mint.
A strength slider blends from pure grayscale (0%) to full duotone (100%).
Processing happens per pixel with the Canvas API — your photo never leaves the browser.
The download is a lossless PNG, rendered at up to 1600 px on the long edge.

limitations: The preview and download are capped at 1600 px on the long edge for performance.
Only two colors are used — true multi-tone or gradient-map effects are not supported.
Transparency (alpha) is preserved but not tinted by the duotone map.
Very low-contrast photos can look muddy; the tool does not auto-enhance contrast first.
